title: High School Math Mentorship Program
text:
The Department of Mathematics at the University of Toronto is proud to offer a mentorship program pairing high school students interested in the field of mathematics study and research, with graduate students, post-doctoral fellows and faculty in the field. Students will be working on a math research project of their interests under the guidance of their mentor.

From January to May, mentees and mentors collaborate to explore a field of mathematical research, guided and supported by faculty members from the Department of Mathematics. The goal of the program is to nurture curiosity and deepen understanding by engaging students in authentic research practices. Strong projects may even contribute novel results or perspectives that advance conversations within a particular area of mathematics.

The program begins with an opening reception to meet all participants in January and ends with a closing ceremony in May to showcase their project to all mentees, mentors and family. Attendance at both events is mandatory, and both will be held in person at the University of Toronto St. George Campus. The top project(s) selected by the evaluation team in May will get an opportunity to attend the Canadian Undergraduate Mathematics Conference to present their research work.

Mentees will meet with their mentors on a regular basis either virtually or at the downtown location of U of T on a schedule that fits both of them about once or twice per month.

Please note this is a highly competitive program and some applicants may not receive a placement.

More information can be found at their website https://www.mathematics.utoronto.ca/outreach/current-programs/grades-1-12-programs/math-mentorship.
